title: Stable signal runs
statement: A stream records integer signal labels from 0 to 100. Find the length of the longest contiguous run containing at most two distinct labels. Return zero for an empty stream. There are at most 100 labels. Do not change the input.

lesson.summary: Expand right and increment its frequency. While more than two labels remain, decrement the left label, remove zero frequencies and advance left. After restoring validity record the maximum window length.
recognition: The output concerns a contiguous run.
A frequency table lets a moving window restore a limit on distinct labels.
Keep left, right, label frequencies, a distinct count and the best valid length.
lesson.invariant: After shrinking, the frequency table describes exactly the current window and it contains at most two distinct labels. Every earlier left boundary discarded for this right boundary would be invalid.
lesson.complexity: O(n + 101) time and O(101) auxiliary space; each boundary advances at most n times.
pitfalls: Counting a window before shrinking can include three labels.
Removing a label from the distinct count before its frequency reaches zero loses repeated labels.
Resetting the whole window on a third label discards useful suffixes.

Place the left-frequency decrement inside while distinct > 2. Decrement distinct only when that frequency reaches zero, then advance left. Complete the best-length update after the while loop.

Reference reasoning: Expand right and increment its frequency. While more than two labels remain, decrement the left label, remove zero frequencies and advance left. After restoring validity record the maximum window length. O(n + 101) time and O(101) auxiliary space; each boundary advances at most n times.

python.solution:
def solve(values):
    counts = [0] * 101
    left = distinct = best = 0
    for right, value in enumerate(values):
        if counts[value] == 0: distinct += 1
        counts[value] += 1
        while distinct > 2:
            counts[values[left]] -= 1
            if counts[values[left]] == 0: distinct -= 1
            left += 1
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best

review.prompt: After expanding to a third distinct label, why may the left pointer need to advance more than once?

options.text: The whole window must be reset whenever a third label appears.
Removing any single label always reduces the distinct count by one.
Removing one occurrence can leave that label elsewhere in the window; shrink until a label frequency becomes zero and validity is restored.

review.rationale: Distinct counts change only when a frequency crosses zero. Several left removals can be needed; record the best length only after restoring at most two labels.
